title: Talia's Tiny Fan Frogs
markdown:
Young Talia Bright, sunny hair and terrier Bracken, was mapping the valley with Dr. Rowan Quill. Special spots: micro-habitats, pockets with their own weather, the sort of places a map lumps together and a frog does not.

No one gathered explorers. The valley did that job by being complicated.

In a steamy corner they found a frog with a fluffy feather fringe around its neck. Miserable. Panting in the heat. The fringe hung limp, a collar with no breeze to employ. Bracken whined, then sneezed, which did not help the frog and did help Talia’s notes: hot / still / unhappy.

They moved to a cooler, breezy patch only a short hop away, as if the valley had installed two rooms and forgotten a door. Here dozens of the same frogs puffed their chests, feathered collars ruffling. Delighted. Talia watched one hop from the hot spot to the breezy one. Its feathers caught the air, fanning the skin. “Whoa. Tiny built-in fans.”

The aha was not magic. The frogs were fitted to different pockets. The feathery collars worked in breeze and were nearly useless in steam. Same species, different comfort, metres apart. Bracken tried the breezy patch and decided he, too, had a niche, which was shade.

Talia scribbled. Bodies, traits, the fit between animal and pocket. She found, on the same transect, birds with beaks like nutcrackers at a hazel stand, insects with sticky feet walking underside of leaves in the damp, burrowers with mini-shovel claws in the loose bank. Each a key for one lock, none of them a speech.

Back at camp Quill beamed. “Specific traits. Adaptations. They fit a niche.” He did not ask what other secrets hid under noses. He poured tea that tasted of the thermos and pointed at Talia’s two frog sketches, hot and fanned.

Talia’s eyes sparkled. She labelled the map steam-pocket and breeze-pocket, taped a shed feather-scale (if that was the word; Quill wrote keratinous fringe) beside the panting sketch, and let Bracken choose the next transect by nose. The valley kept its two weathers. The frogs, given a choice, voted for the fan.
